title: Structural span ranges
description: Select the framing systems that can span a given distance, and explain why a longer span usually means a deeper, costlier, or more specialized system.
creator: The Science of the Built Environment
author: Dan McCreary
subject: The Science of the Built Environment

timeless: Deflection grows with the fourth power of the span, so doubling a span needs far more depth or stiffness.
Longer spans trade simple, cheap members for deeper, engineered, or prefabricated ones.

ages.item: Every span range on the chart
ages.basis: Illustrative round numbers from general design references; the chapters do not give them
ages.check: Use the manufacturer's span tables or an engineer's calculation for a real project

ages.item: Which systems exist as stock products
ages.basis: Common products at the time of writing
ages.check: Confirm availability and depth limits with local suppliers

pedagogical.learningObjective: Select the framing systems that can span a given distance, and explain why a longer span usually means a deeper, costlier, or more specialized system.
recommendedUsage: Move the slider, or drag the red marker in the chart, to a span you care about. The headline counts how many systems reach it.
Look at the dark bars first. A system in its typical range is an ordinary choice; one in the light part of its bar is possible but unusual and usually costs more.
Click a system's name to read what it is, why you would choose it, and what to watch out for.
Untick Wood, Steel, or Concrete to compare one material at a time, and change Sort to rank the systems by how far they reach.

Drag the red marker, or use the slider under the chart, to set your own span. Rows that reach it stay dark; rows that do not fade out. Click a row's name for what it is, why to choose it, and what to watch out for.
activities: Predict and test (10 min): before using the chart, list which systems you think can carry the 40 ft Riverbend girder, then check.
Compare (10 min): find the span at which wood framing stops being typical and steel takes over. Explain what changes for the building at that point.
Apply (10 min): choose a floor system for a 28 ft clear span with ducts running through it and justify the choice.
assessment: Name three systems that can span 40 ft and say which are typical at that span.
Explain in two sentences why a sawn lumber joist cannot be the answer for a 30 ft span.
